First NEXUS infrastructure review to assess Atlas-2 capacity, working storage, backups and isolation requirements for evaluation and project data.

Clara Ibáñez: The all-hands meeting identified storage expansion as a priority. Nuria, present the current status.
Nuria Castaño: Atlas-2 has 320 raw terabytes. The fast tier is at 81 percent, the archive tier at 63 percent and external backups consume 54 percent of the contracted quota.
Sergio Vidal: Part of the growth comes from duplicate corpora and containers without retention policies.
Andrés Beltrán: ARIADNA needs test sets to be physically separated or protected through strong permissions. They must not remain in directories shared with experiments.
Elena Martín: SILEX and LUMEN also need to retain versions and evidence, but not everything requires fast storage.
Nuria Castaño: I propose three immediate measures: automated lifecycle management, an additional 80 terabytes of fast storage and an encrypted area for restricted data.
Sergio Vidal: Backups must be tested through restoration, not only through successful-job logs.
Clara Ibáñez: What are the estimated schedule and cost for the expansion?
Nuria Castaño: Procurement before 15 March and commissioning during April. The cost fits the infrastructure budget if we postpone two non-critical GPUs.
Elena Martín: Approved. We will retain one planned GPU for the second half of the year and prioritize storage, isolation and restoration.
Clara Ibáñez: I will record the budget change and quarterly recovery test.
